prompt: Two forms share some validation code. A junior wants to build a shared form framework; the senior says to copy it for now and wait for a third form.
tells: copy it for now and wait for a third form
why: With two cases, you don't yet know the right abstraction.
trap: Close to YAGNI, but the cue is waiting for the third repeat.

prompt: A shared helper written after the second use now has nine flags, because every new caller differs a little.
tells: written after the second use now has nine flags
why: Abstracting too early locks in the wrong shape.
trap: It's debt now, but the mistake was abstracting at two.

prompt: The same retry loop shows up for the third time in the codebase, so the engineer pulls it into one function.
tells: shows up for the third time
why: Three real cases show what to share.
trap: It's cleanup, but the cue is the third repeat.

prompt: A reviewer flags two similar 10-line functions as a DRY violation. The author replies that they may diverge and it's too early to merge them.
tells: it's too early to merge them
why: A little duplication beats a premature abstraction.
trap: It's a disagreement, but the content is when to abstract.

prompt: A team inlines a shared base class back into its two users, because each needs different behavior and the base had grown tangled.
tells: inlines a shared base class back into its two users
why: Undo an abstraction made before the pattern was clear.
trap: It reduces debt, but the lesson is about premature abstraction.

prompt: A tech lead tells the team: some copy-paste is fine; extract shared code once you have three real examples.
tells: once you have three real examples
trap: It's advice from a lead, but the advice is the pattern.
